# whatever the call is unified with — and, inside a generator's
# template, by the source child the generated one is made FROM.
# BREAKING CHANGE, pinned here. A bare `_` used to be the string "_";
# it is a hole now. `"_"` quoted is still that string, a longer bare
# word containing it is still ordinary text, and `_` as a KEY is still
# a key — the four rows that say so are the compatibility contract.
# The peer goes INTO the call and is not also a constraint on the way
# out: `upper(_) & hello` is "HELLO", not "HELLO" & "hello". Two holes
# meeting is an error, because neither has a value to fill the other.
# A hole under a PREFERENCE: the generated default is the source
# child, still overridable per child. This is the row that reaches the
# pref arm of the fill walk, whose peg is a Val rather than a list of
# The fill walk reaches every shape a template can hold: a conjunct, a
# disjunct, a list, a nested map — and two placeheld OPERATORS meeting
# is the same refusal two placeheld calls are.
# The hole fills with 1, leaving `1|string`: two alternatives still
# admitted, so incomplete residue rather than a scalar conflict
# A HOLE BELONGS TO ITS NEAREST ENCLOSING GENERATOR (ADR-005,
# 2026-08-26; use-cases/BUGS.md §34): an outer pack's fill pass used
# to fill a NESTED pack's template hole lexically, binding `_` to the
# OUTER source child — deploy.dev.services.web.v answered the env name
# "dev", exit 0. Each generator now fills only its own template's
# holes: the inner `_` is the inner generator's source child, both as
# a bare hole and as a meet operand. Parity-probed in both engines.
# A HOLE AS A GENERATOR'S DATA (the other side of the boundary): the
# first hole in `each(_, _)` is in the DATA argument — a binding
# position it is NOT — so the OUTER pack's fill pass fills it with the
# outer source child, and the inner each() then iterates that child
# (its own hole, the second, stays its own). The two-arg
# spelling pins that the inner TEMPLATE argument rides through the
# fill untouched. Parity-probed in both engines.
# A rider, a mark or a seal around a container that holds a hole reads
# through to it, so the peer meets the container member by member. A
# seal around a rider seals the container the rider wraps, so it still
# refuses a key the peer adds, and a rider's record settles first. A
# rider's record is a container argument, so a hole in it is the
# record's, which the peer leaves unfilled.
# A call waits on a hole among its own arguments, and through a call or
# a rider among them, but not on one a container argument holds: that
# hole is the container's, which its own meet fills. So the peer leaves
# it unfilled, and a call that computes from its arguments' values fails
# once they settle, as it can't be made. A join stands, as the
# definition reads it. Where the call waits on a hole of its own as
# well, the peer fills that one alone, and a container met with a
# waiting call is the call's argument, not a second hole.
# A held hole no meet reaches fails the call though another argument
# still waits, here on a path to a hole. A call that takes its argument
# as the value it is reads a list or a map that holds a hole as that
# container, so its peer fills the hole, and a bound reads one as outside
# its domain; but neq reads the members as the values it refuses, so a
# hole among them is one nothing fills. super reads a call there that
# waits on its own hole as any, so a hole beside one is what stays
# unmade; a bound whose list also holds such a call waits still.
# A spread whose template leaves a hole member unfilled keeps its
# container unsettled, so a call over it is never made.
# A held hole under a choice of arms leaves the call over its container
# unmade: a call, a `+`, a map and a list there, each held as written.
# A call over a container whose argument is the hole takes its peer as
# that argument, as any call does, and computes from it once the peer
# settles: on either side, over a map, for each such call, and with the
# hole as `join`'s separator. A peer the call refuses is refused as the
# A grammar call takes its peer as the hole it waits on, as any call
# does: abnf's grammar, and either of parse's two arguments. A text the
# grammar refuses is refused as the argument.
# A map spread's container template meets each member once, as a list
# spread's does: a member it has filled meets a later value as it
# stands, so the template's call is never applied to its own output.
# The template still constrains what a later value adds to the member.

# A meet that fills a hole inside a size, a trial or a match settles as
# it would written filled, so the size or trial it stands in reads its
# value: in len, must, a match's scrutinee and its pattern, contains and
# `+` joins two lists as they stand, whatever their elements hold, so a
# hole an operand list holds is the joined list's, which the meet fills
# member by member: on either side, from a longer list and a shorter
# one, with a hole in each operand, met again and through a second `+`.
# Left unmet, the hole stands where the join puts it. The lists join once
# only their holes wait, so a `key()` an operand list holds reads where
# it's written, in that list. The `+` waits only on a hole among its
# operands, which its peer fills alone, so a hole an operand list holds
# A member that waits only on a hole joins too: a choice with a hole
# among its arms, or a meet with a hole beside a value still being made.
# A map with a spread joins once it's made, here once its path resolves.
# A call over a hole in an operand list of `+` meets its member once the
# lists are joined, and the meet fills it: on either side of the meet,
# in the right list, inside a map, in both lists, and from a shorter
# peer. Met again, the filled member conflicts with the peer's. A `key()`
# reads its index where it's written, in either list, and a list's spread
# meets its elements before the lists join.
